name: ccv (BBF face detector)
baseline: OpenCV default frontal face detector (Haar cascade, default settings; OpenCV version not stated)
workload: ccv bbfdetect versus OpenCV's face detector run over the CMU/MIT frontal face test sets A, B and C (images converted to PNG, one file list), timed with `time` on the same computer.
claimed_speedup: bbfdetect real 0m9.304s versus OpenCV default face detector real 0m27.977s (about 3.0x faster, derived from page data). doc/scd.rst: 'OpenCV is about 3 times slower than BBF with single thread setup' and SCD (the BBF successor) is 'only twice as slow as BBF', so SCD is roughly 1.5x faster than OpenCV (derived from page data). Accuracy trade on the CMU sets: BBF 82.97% detection with 12 false alarms versus OpenCV 86.69% with 15.
hardware: Author's own computer, CPU not stated
tradeoffs: C library with few dependencies and a tiny-footprint detector; BBF gives up some detection rate against OpenCV's Haar cascade on the CMU sets (82.97% vs 86.69%); on FDDB at about 250 false positives doc/scd.rst puts BBF at 66.27% and OpenCV's frontal detector at 45.18%. Code is BSD-3-Clause, but COPYING says ./doc, ./samples (trained models) and ./site are CC BY 4.0.
caveats: First-party doc with a single `time` run: no CPU model, compiler or flags, OpenCV version and program not named, OpenCV at default settings (not matched to bbfdetect's scale and neighbour parameters), run includes image decoding and output, and the test data is from the OpenCV 2.x era. doc/bbf.rst opens with a Deprecated notice: BBF is 'no longer considered either fast or accurate' as of libccv 0.7 and was to be replaced by SCD, though lib and bin code are still in the repo. Same record already exists from wave 1 (w1-mine-a, https://github.com/liuliu/ccv in wave1/verified.json); this seed pass reached the same numbers independently. The ccv unstable branch now also carries first-party Metal/ANE int8 attention benchmarks (MFADecoding.md, doc/benchmarks) against ccv's own FP16 NAAttention and a 'generic/MPS' path with no hardware stated; not used here. ccv's own dpm.rst reports OpenCV's HOG detector 4.34x faster than ccv's DPM, and convnet.rst says ccv chooses correctness over speed, so the claim covers only the BBF/SCD face detectors.
found_via: seed-record pass: awesome-cpp#Machine Learning listing 'C-based/Cached/Core Computer Vision Library'; evidence from doc/bbf.rst and doc/scd.rst on github.com/liuliu/ccv (unstable branch)
